claims.text: The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is derived by removing Co from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The as-solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is a single-phase FCC solid solution.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi crystallizes as a single-phase FCC solid solution.
Removing Co eliminates the magnetic interactions relevant to deformation in FeNiCrMn.
Magnetic interactions can influence FCC-to-HCP transformation during deformation in concentrated Co-containing alloys.
In parent CoCrFeMnNi, Co-associated magnetic interactions promote a deformation-induced FCC-to-HCP transformation.
In parent CoCrFeMnNi, Co-associated magnetic interactions promote twin nucleation.
Suppressing transformation and twinning in Co-free FeNiCrMn makes dislocation slip the sole dominant deformation mechanism.
At low temperatures and high strain rates, thermal activation and dynamic recovery in Co-free FeNiCrMn are reduced.
Low temperatures and high strain rates produce dislocation pile-ups in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Reduced recovery and absent transformation-induced hardening cause enhanced strain-rate sensitivity and dynamic softening in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
At low temperatures, increasing strain rate causes a sharper drop in yield strength and flow stress in Co-free FeNiCrMn than in CoCrFeMnNi.
At higher temperatures, thermal activation narrows the dynamic-strength difference between Co-free FeNiCrMn and CoCrFeMnNi.
The strength-ductility balance of CoCrFeMnNi benefits from Co-induced magnetic stabilization and deformation-induced transformation or twinning.
The proposed behavior is limited to an as-solidified, single-phase FCC state without precipitation or significant ordering.
Processing that changes phase stability or introduces secondary phases may cause deviations from the proposed behavior.
The proposed controlled comparison uses identically processed FeNiCrMn and CoCrFeMnNi specimens tested over the same temperature and strain-rate matrix.
Failure to observe a stronger strain-rate dependence and sharper low-temperature strength drop in FeNiCrMn than in CoCrFeMnNi would falsify the proposed mechanism.
